text:
Maria Gomez: Quick follow-up on the offline/air-gapped packaging RFC — proposing a 'parallel component-apply + per-component heal + central supervisor' pattern. TL;DR: allow independent components to apply in parallel, mark per-component activation markers, run a verifier/healer for missing blobs, then a single commit fence to mark the whole bundle activated. Need feedback on locking model, rollback granularity, and operator UX.

Ajay Patel: +1 for parallelism but worried about cross-component dependencies and racey post-install steps. We need a DAG-aware scheduler and per-component prechecks before starting apply. :thinking:

Kim Nguyen: I like a two-phase apply: 1) dry-run (hash/signature checks, disk space, preflight hooks), 2) apply using DAG topo order but permit independent subgraphs to run concurrently. Prechecks must be idempotent.

Leo Park: Healer concern: in air-gapped sites the healer cannot fetch missing blobs from the internet. We should either: bundle minimal heal payloads in the delta, or expose an operator-driven seed mechanism (USB / airgap mirror). Timeouts need to be conservative.

Tara Singh: Rollback granularity note — if we keep the commit fence (single atomic marker) then any component-level rollback is safe until that fence is written. After fence, we need a rollforward/compensating plan. Operator UX: surface per-component "safe_to_rollback" boolean in console. :thumbsup:

Ajay Patel: Example simple manifest graph to reason about race conditions:
```
component-a -> component-b
component-c
component-b -> component-d
```
We should treat each arrow as a hard dependency (b cannot apply until a finished). Independent nodes (component-c) can run in parallel. Use advisory per-component locks (stored in control-plane CR or etcd).

Maria Gomez: On commit fence semantics: propose a commitID record in the control-plane DB that's only written after all verifiers report success. Until commitID written, operator can trigger rollback of any partially-applied component. The write must be atomic and durable across control-plane restarts.

ops-bot: deploy-checker: node-347 reported missing blob sha256:abc123 — healer fallback not configured for that cluster.

Kim Nguyen: To address that, we should include a 'heal payload' bundle in the delta for commonly-missed blobs and an operator flag to allow fetching from a predefined offline mirror. The bundle increases size but improves resilience.

Leo Park: Tests we need: partial-power-loss during parallel apply, verifier crash/restart, missing-blob + heal-bundle present vs absent, and commit-fence race. Also add e2e that simulates stuck post-install hooks.

Tara Singh: UI suggestion: per-component progress bar, a "healing required" badge next to components that failed verification, and a global "commit" button that is disabled until all verifiers pass or operator explicitly overrides (with warning). Include audit log links.

Maria Gomez: OK — next steps: I'll update the RFC with: DAG-aware scheduler design, two-phase apply flow, commit fence semantics (atomic commitID), heal-payload inclusion options, operator seed/mirror patterns, and a test matrix + runbook. Will post a patch for review by EOD. Please respond with a quick +1 / concerns in-thread. Thanks all. :rocket:
